title: Beige Book — July 15, 2026
html:
Official report: Summary · Full PDF Local PDF: 2026-07-15 Beige Book.pdf

Overall economic activity

Activity grew slightly to moderately in eleven of twelve Districts and was flat in one. Manufacturing grew modestly to moderately, led by data center, machinery, and defense orders, though supply chain problems became more common. Construction and real estate edged up, with data center building a notable driver. Lending rose modestly, while consumer loan quality slipped slightly. Agriculture weakened on lower commodity prices, higher input costs, and tighter credit. Contacts expect continued expansion but flagged uncertainty about fuel costs.

Consumer spending

Consumer spending rose modestly, but shoppers pulled back on discretionary goods because of higher fuel prices. Tourism improved, helped by World Cup visitors.

Labor markets

Employment rose overall: five Districts reported modest or larger gains and seven were roughly flat. Skilled trades and technical roles were hard to fill. Wage growth was modest to moderate, and some firms used AI in hiring or to raise productivity.

Prices

Prices rose moderately overall, and price growth was the same or slower than the prior period in every District. Input costs climbed for services, construction, and manufacturing, tied to energy, transportation, raw materials, the Middle East conflict, and tariffs. Some firms could not pass all of these costs on, squeezing margins. Inflation expectations varied, with some contacts expecting easing as fuel prices fall.

Notable themes

  • Data centers: driving both manufacturing orders and construction.
  • Energy/fuel: still the key cost and consumer headwind, but some expect relief.
  • Defense: supporting manufacturing orders.
  • Supply chains: problems became more common.
  • Tourism/World Cup: a boost to travel.
  • AI: used in hiring and for productivity.

District highlights

  • Boston: Slight expansion; flat employment; discretionary spending softened among lower- and middle-income households.
  • New York: Modest growth; services picking up; firms more optimistic.
  • Philadelphia: Slight growth; nonmanufacturing improved; employment dipped slightly.
  • Cleveland: Modest growth; manufacturing demand up, retail soft; selling prices rose quickly.
  • Richmond: Moderate expansion; consumer spending grew; manufacturing up modestly.
  • Atlanta: Modest growth; flat employment; agriculture worsened; lending up modestly.
  • Chicago: Modest growth; manufacturing up moderately; financial conditions tightened slightly; farm income expectations edged down.
  • St. Louis: Slight growth; flat employment; prices rose at a robust pace.
  • Minneapolis: Slight growth; employment up modestly; agriculture deteriorated.
  • Kansas City: Slight growth led by manufacturing; inflation squeezed margins.
  • Dallas: Moderate growth; energy and services strengthened, manufacturing slowed; employment improved.
  • San Francisco: Stable but muted; headcounts steady; investment in AI; retail and services edged down.

Read-through for SPY

  • Broadest growth of the year so far (eleven of twelve Districts) with employment rising is a constructive backdrop for earnings.
  • Price growth steady or slower everywhere is a welcome sign for rates and valuations.
  • Data center and defense demand remain the clearest sector tailwinds; discretionary retail still faces fuel-price pressure.
